Compactness of near-minimizers and positivity of sufficiently small tangent paths rigorously identify finite-step first-order infima. All-ones Rayleigh equality uniquely forces balanced weights; exact eigenvalues yield the sharp interval. Reflection convexity proves global half-spread optimality at u=1/2, exact eigenvalues and the two-point obstruction give all constants. Included exact symbolic verifier checks critical algebra; finite cases are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Spectral operator errors and conditioning drive worst-case numerical stability; mean-square Frobenius minimization does not solve them. The theorem delivers a sharp quantitative phase interval for reaching a universal best operator norm, exact and conflicting correction rules for operator and condition-number objectives, and a proof that 3 is the minimum DFT dimension permitting any spectral gain. These are motivated diagnostic boundaries rather than arbitrary sampled constants; scope is strictly finite-dimensional and first-order.
